title: Find Median from Data Stream
description: Two heaps: a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, kept balanced. addNum O(log n), findMedian O(1).

notes: Invariant: every value in `lo` is <= every value in `hi`, and `lo.size() - hi.size()` is 0 or 1.
Route incoming n by comparing to `lo.peek()`; then rebalance by transferring at most one element.
If total count is odd, `lo` holds the extra and `lo.peek()` is the median. If even, average the two roots.

questions.q: Why use a MAX-heap for the lower half and a MIN-heap for the upper half?
options: So the two heap roots are the median candidates

questions.q: When the two heaps have equal size, the median is:

exercises.prompt: Fill in the routing and median formula. Heaps are provided.

blanks.hint: smaller-or-equal values go to the lower half
everything else goes to the upper half

L3.prompt: Implement `MedianFinder` with `addNum(n)` and `findMedian()`. Use two inline heaps (max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper half). After adding 1,2,3,4 with a findMedian after each pair, log the running medians.
hints: Implement MinHeap and MaxHeap with push (sift-up) and pop (sift-down) operations using an array.
Route n into `lo` if n <= lo.peek(), else into `hi`, then rebalance so |lo.size - hi.size| <= 1 with lo never smaller.
Median: if lo larger, return lo.peek(); else average the two roots.
